methodological_rigor.justification: Large national precision-oncology cohort (N=3383) with prospective enrollment, algorithmic tiering via TOPOGRAPH to minimize subjective bias, and time-dependent multivariable Cox regression to address immortal time bias. Prespecified stratification into cohort A (no further therapy) and cohort B (received therapy) aids interpretation. Sensitivity analyses address patients who died before profiling and use of updated TOPOGRAPH tiering. Main limitation is observational design; no comparison with other tiering frameworks (e.g., ESCAT) and residual confounding by indication possible.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Demonstrates that genomic therapy matching only produces survival benefit when supported by prospective trial evidence (tiers 1-3A: aHR 0.60), cautioning against off-label repurposing (tier 3B: aHR 1.40). These findings directly inform precision oncology practice, molecular tumor board decisions, and reimbursement debates. Individual prospective cohort -> Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: Authors explicitly state STROBE adherence, provide ANZCTR registration (ACTRN12616000908437), detailed eligibility, tiering methodology, algorithmic tier assignment, time-dependent Cox model, and multiple sensitivity analyses. Ethics approval and informed consent documented. Data availability statement not visible in normalized text (likely in supplement).

novelty_literature.justification: First large cohort to prospectively operationalize the TOPOGRAPH tiering framework across a rare/refractory cancer population (71.7% rare cancers) and empirically demonstrate that only tier 1-3A matches confer survival benefit. Extends prior precision-oncology programs (MOSCATO, SHIVA, WINTHER, TAPUR, MyPathway, NCI-MATCH) by providing an evidence-based decision framework. Meaningful novel contribution to implementation science in precision oncology.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured with clear stratification of cohorts, explicit tier definitions, and candid interpretation. The distinction between clinically active (tiers 1-3A) and investigational (tiers 3B/4) matches is communicated clearly, and the surprising tier 3B aHR 1.40 is discussed. Figures and tables are well signposted. Limitations and implications for drug access are thoughtfully framed.

key_strengths: Large national cohort (N=3383) with 71.7% rare cancers, addressing a population underrepresented in RCTs
Algorithmic TOPOGRAPH tiering minimizes subjective bias and allows reproducible stratification
Time-dependent Cox regression addresses immortal time bias
Clinically actionable finding: only prospective-trial-supported matches (tiers 1-3A) confer survival benefit (aHR 0.60)
Noteworthy signal against off-label repurposing (tier 3B aHR 1.40) with plausible delay-to-therapy explanation
key_concerns: Observational design with residual confounding by treatment selection and drug access
Tier 3B finding is clinically consequential but rests on a relatively small subgroup
No head-to-head comparison with ESCAT or OncoKB frameworks
Only 3.4% of eligible patients actually received tier 1-3A matched therapy, limiting generalizability
Data availability statement not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality precision-oncology implementation study with an important, clinically actionable finding about evidence-based therapy matching; appropriate for a Tier 1 venue such as JAMA Oncology or JAMA given scope, clinical relevance, and rigorous time-dependent analysis.
